explicit_validation.explanation: The paper explicitly validates LLM-as-a-judge against human evaluation by comparing GPT-4's sub-question coverage judgments with human annotations on 100 samples and reports alignment rate; also compares LLM-as-a-judge pairwise evaluation with human preference data.

prompts.notes: Prompts not fully shown but described: For sub-question coverage judgment, GPT-4 is prompted to judge if text contains answer to sub-question and identify relevant text fragments; for pairwise evaluation, GPT-4 is directly prompted to compare two responses.

guidelines.notes: Guidelines include definitions of three sub-question types with examples; human preference annotations from WebGPT Comparisons dataset used with preference scores mapped to labels.

sample_size.notes: Validation uses 100 samples for sub-question coverage alignment and 500 samples for answer quality preference comparison

quantitative_scores.notes: Alignment rate between GPT-4 automatic judgments and human annotations on 100 samples
Core sub-question coverage metric accuracy compared to human preference annotations
Weighted hybrid metric (core:1, background:0.5, follow-up:-1) accuracy compared to human preference

validation_results.summary_finding: GPT-4 achieves 83% agreement with human annotations on sub-question coverage; sub-question coverage metrics (78-82% accuracy) outperform standard LLM-as-a-judge approach in matching human preferences.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM evaluates sub-question coverage and pairwise comparisons; humans evaluate sub-question type classification and answer preferences; both evaluate sub-question coverage and overall answer quality preferences
